html:
A free, open source operating system kernel first released on 17 September 1991 by Linus Torvalds, then a student at the University of Helsinki in Finland. A kernel is the core of an operating system: the part that talks to the hardware.

Torvalds started it as a hobby, a free alternative to Unix for his own PC. He posted it online and invited others to help. Joined with the tools of the GNU Project and released under its licence, which lets anyone use and change the code if they share their changes, it became a complete system built by thousands of volunteers and companies.

Linux now runs most web servers, the Android phones in most people's pockets, and all of the world's fastest supercomputers. It is the clearest proof that open, shared work can build software as big as anything made by firms, and much of the web runs on it.
